original_card.question: Can one specified masked or overcomplete decoder improve the complete moment budget?
methods: Synthesize a decoder with exact coefficients and fully priced helper endpoints.
Bound the best possible budget for a fixed support alphabet before synthesis.
original_card.acceptance_gate: Change an assumption of the eight-term all-pairs bound and count all copied information, frames and restoration.

first_step.inspect: Locate the excluded classes: masked identities, at least nine terms, and deeper punctures.
first_step.scope: Positive control / source-bound orientation only; this is not a new construction or full cold replay.

original_card.first_experiment: Choose one finite support alphabet and test exact decoding constraints before building a whole network.
original_card.bottleneck_link: A cheaper fully realized decoder could increase deficit or lower recursive cost on the binding complex side.
allowed_variations: Select a specific masked or overcomplete family with exact labels and supports.
scope_change_triggers: Repeating the exact eight-term all-pairs search inside its proved scope.

actual_scope: Proof obligation inside the masked (E-graph) model: is every rank-<=8 solution of PR1212's system (E) on P112 minus X, for the 198688 triples X not inside a P112 frame (the part of P109 that PR1419's extension lemma cannot reach), equal to D(2G)D^-1, so that decoders with exactly eight costly terms keep PR968's floor 61 on every P109 unit?
scope_change_reason: The card asks whether a masked decoder can beat the floor. PR1212/PR1389/PR1399 answered it for exactly eight costly terms on P120, P112, P111 and every P104 frame complement, PR1419 for punctures inside a frame, and PR1425 for the rest of P110; PR1425's open next question is P109. This closes it; it does not construct a decoder.
bottleneck_link: Side result on the binding complex supplier: masked eight-costly-term decoders cannot beat PR968's floor on any P109 unit, so the remaining masked escape routes are nine or more costly terms or punctures of depth four or more not inside a frame.
stop_rule: Stop at P109 with one PR; P108 (168 open orbits, trial run only) and deeper punctures, and nine or more costly terms, are left as handoffs.
evidence: verify.py: 25 exact checks in about 15 s (generators; triple orbit census with the inside-a-frame split; one unit per open orbit; per unit the pivot's D4 structure, (I3), (I4) and gluing, Lemma 9 connectivity and algebra, assembly, CNF consistency, DRUP replay of zero exclusion with its own RUP checker and the needs-zero-clause control; one bogus-proof control). PR1212's rup_check independently accepts all 19 proofs, and an independently written census (OpenAI Codex, from a specification) matches the orbit table (both recorded, not run by verify.py); a read-only adversarial review by OpenAI Codex found no soundness gap (not a human review).

open_questions.question: Does rank-8 rigidity of (E) hold on P108 units P112 minus X, |X| = 4, where X is not inside a frame of P112 (168 of 180 orbits, 6132952 of 6210820 quadruples)?
open_questions.why_it_matters: With this package and PR1419 every P109 unit is rigid; P108 is the next depth of the eight-term gap in the masked model.
open_questions.first_step: A trial run of make_proof.py's pivot rule and CNF on all 168 representatives found a passing pivot and an UNSAT CNF for each (361027 lemmas, about 5.9 MB gzipped); package it with a census of 4-subsets.
open_questions.blocked_by: Proof volume and a pure-Python census of 6.2 million quadruples; orbit counts keep growing toward P105 (order 1e5 orbits), so a structural replacement for the DRUP zero-exclusion step is needed to go deep.
